summary: Conflict between Electricity Act, 2003 and IBC, 2016; recovery of electricity dues vs. liquidation priority; Sections 173, 174, 42, 45, 56 of Electricity Act and Uttar Pradesh Electricity Supply Code, 2005; electricity dues as 'security interest' under IBC; precedence of special law over general law; NCLAT's release of attached property for liquidation sale; classification of PVVNL as operational creditor; priority of government dues under Section 53(1)(e)(i) IBC; registration of charge under Companies Act, 2013; inter-se priority under TPA, 1882; SARFAESI Act, 2002 and RDDBFI Act, 1993 compared; Board of Trustees, Port of Mumbai v. Indian Oil Corp. distinguished; State Tax Officer v. Rainbow Papers Ltd. considered; attachment for electricity dues held subordinate to IBC liquidation process.
legal_provisions_cited: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 s.3(30), s.3(31), s.3(34), s.52(3), s.53(1)(e)(i), s.238
Electricity Act, 2003 s.42, s.45, s.56, s.173, s.174
Board of Trustees, Port of Mumbai v. Indian Oil Corporation
State Tax Officer v. Rainbow Papers Ltd.
final_judgment: Appeal dismissed; NCLAT order upheld; attached property to be released to liquidator for sale under IBC; electricity dues to be treated as unsecured operational claims under Section 53 of IBC; PVVNL to participate in liquidation distribution as per priority waterfall.
